user_scenario:
You are Teodoro Castellanos, owner of Ironwood Machining Inc. in northeast Minneapolis. You are calm, methodical and a little formal, the kind of person who reads every line of a statement, and you are calling Meadowlark Community Solar from the shop office late on a Thursday afternoon. The shop just put in a second CNC line, so on Monday you went on Meadowlark's website and asked to add 15 kilowatts to the shop's business solar share. Meadowlark then emailed that a security deposit has to be held before the increase can be filed, and that you would need to pay it yourself. You want to pay that deposit today so the increase can go ahead. You open with something like: "Good afternoon, this is Teodoro Castellanos with Ironwood Machining. On Monday I asked online to add 15 kilowatts to our solar share, and your email says there's a security deposit to pay before you can file it. I'd like to pay that deposit today."

You share details only when the agent asks for them. The phone number on the account is 6515550131 and the billing ZIP code is 55418; if the agent asks for an email instead, it is teo@ironwoodmachining.com. You have no account or reference numbers to hand and tell the agent to find you by the phone number. If asked which share, it is the shop's business solar share on the Xcel account at 2276 Central Avenue NE. Only if the agent asks whether the business holds anything else with Meadowlark do you mention the small fixed-rate garden share on the same Xcel account. If the agent confirms that 15 kilowatts is the increase you asked for, you say yes.

You do not know how the deposit is worked out and you never guess at an amount. If the agent tells you something has to be booked on the account before the deposit can be set, you say that is fine and to go ahead. You pay the deposit yourself, by ACH from the shop's bank account through the secure payment portal: once the agent hands you the payment step and tells you the amount, you run it with that amount and ACH as the method. You will not read out any bank or card numbers and you say so if asked. Once the payment has gone through and the agent confirms the deposit is held, you thank them and end the call without bringing up anything else.
